justification: The sitemap advertised two URLs that returned 404, and nothing checked. Adds redirects plus a guard covering all 44 static sitemap entries.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A static ${base}/path entry in sitemap.ts has neither a page.tsx that maps to it (route groups resolved) nor a matching redirect source in next.config.js.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Removing the /shadow redirect: 1 failed, 44 passed. Removing the /solar-potential redirect: 1 failed, 44 passed. Renaming a sitemap entry to a route that does not exist: 1 failed, 44 passed. Each kills exactly one case. Baseline and restored both 45 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: 44 static sitemap entries in chunk 0. Measured live on verify.plotdetect.com.au WITHOUT following redirects, which is the distinction that mattered: /flood-risk and /threat-radar return 307 and were fine; /shadow and /solar-potential returned a direct 404. Following redirects had earlier made /flood-risk look identical to a working page and hid the difference.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I assumed the two dead pages needed building. They did not - next.config.js already had clean-URL redirects for the same tools under DIFFERENT slugs, /shadow-check and /solar-yield. The sitemap named /shadow and /solar-potential. Nothing reconciled the two lists, so the mismatch was invisible. The fix is two lines, not two pages.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies at next deploy. Crawlers that already recorded a 404 for these URLs will re-resolve on the next crawl.

functions.name: routeExists
functions.input: A URL path such as /reports/flood, taken from a static sitemap entry.
functions.output: True if some page.tsx maps to that path. Descends into (group) folders without consuming a path segment, since a route group does not appear in the URL.
functions.if_none: Returns false. A resolver that always returned false would make every case fail and a broken one that always returned true would make the guard useless, so a separate test pins both directions against a known-good and a known-bad path.
functions.why: Route groups are why a naive directory check is wrong here: /shadow lives at app/(tools)/shadow, so the (tools) segment must be skipped rather than matched.

functions.name: staticSitemapPaths
functions.input: No arguments. Reads app/sitemap.ts and matches ${base}/path template literals.
functions.output: Sorted unique static paths, excluding '/' and any entry containing an interpolation.
functions.if_none: An empty list would pass every case vacuously, so a separate assertion requires more than ten entries before the per-path checks are trusted.
functions.why: Only the hand-typed entries can drift. The LGA chunks map a slug array onto a [lga-slug] route, so their shape is guaranteed by construction.

break_it.scenario: A sitemap entry names a page that does not exist.
break_it.what_happens: Crawl budget is spent on a URL that returns 404, and the sitemap is reported back as containing errors. It is worse than never listing the page, and it persisted here because a sitemap is never opened by a human.
break_it.how: Every static entry is checked against the route tree and the redirect table.
break_it.repro: Rename a sitemap entry to a nonexistent route -> 1 failed, 44 passed

break_it.scenario: A clean URL is added under one slug while the sitemap advertises another.
break_it.what_happens: Exactly what happened: redirects existed for /shadow-check and /solar-yield while the sitemap said /shadow and /solar-potential. Both lists looked correct in isolation.
break_it.how: The guard reads BOTH files and requires the sitemap's own slug to resolve, so the two can no longer disagree silently.

break_it.scenario: The resolver breaks and reports everything as fine.
break_it.what_happens: A guard that always returns true is worse than none, because it certifies the thing it stopped checking.
break_it.how: A test asserts routeExists('/assessment') is true AND routeExists('/definitely-not-a-route') is false, pinning both directions.
break_it.repro: Make routeExists return true unconditionally -> the known-bad assertion fails

post_merge.manual_verify: After deploy, confirm /shadow and /solar-potential return 307 rather than 404. The redirect only takes effect at build time, so the current 404 persists until then.
